claims: "All for Alex" is an annual SEC-wide campaign.
"All for Alex" honors late Mississippi State player Alex Wilcox.
Alex Wilcox passed away from ovarian cancer in 2018 at age 18.
The purpose of "All for Alex" is to honor Alex Wilcox.
The purpose of "All for Alex" is to raise awareness for ovarian cancer.
The purpose of "All for Alex" is to spread the message that "No One Fights Alone".
"All for Alex" was created by LSU coach Beth Torina and MSU coach Samantha Ricketts.
SEC softball teams wear teal during a designated weekend.
Teal is the color representing ovarian cancer awareness.
"All for Alex" has expanded beyond the SEC to include other universities.
Alex Wilcox was a Mississippi State freshman in 2018.
Alex Wilcox continued to play while battling cancer.
Mississippi State retired Alex Wilcox's No. 8 jersey.
Alex Wilcox is the first female student-athlete in Mississippi State school history to have her jersey retired.
"All for Alex" educates people about the symptoms of ovarian cancer including bloating, cramping, and back pain.
"All for Alex" has been recognized with the SEC Sportsmanship Award.
